item: A URL's userinfo is out of a link's domain label, the feed key, the canonical URL and the feed preflight's host, read after the last @ as the fetcher does (R628)
summary: R628 (Plan 01:53Z: fold the userinfo labels into R621's masking, a follow-up after R624, with two security reads and a test that the canonical key dedupes the credentialed and plain forms of one URL; the four places are R624's row's 'same pattern elsewhere' list). Each now reads a URL's host as the fetcher does: what follows the LAST @ of the authority, as urllib.parse reads it. BEFORE: (1) src/services/link_analyzer/extractor.py kept the userinfo in a link's domain label (main path, regex fallback, and the label the social/ad/tracking substring checks search), so https://twitter.com:x@news.example/a read as social, and internal against external compared two whole netlocs, so a link to the page's own host written with a userinfo, a port or www. read as external and was stored as an outbound ArticleLink, credentials included; (2) src/database/feed_key.py kept the userinfo in the feed identity, so one feed written with and without credentials was two sources; (3) src/utils/url_utils.py kept it in canonicalize_url, get_domain_from_url and get_base_url, so the dedup read one page as two (a crawl from a credentialed start fetched the page again without them) and the credentials reached the stored canonical_url; (4) src/monitoring/feed_preflight.py put it in a report's host field, and the robots read built from that host sent it (requests turns it into Authorization: Basic). NOW: (1) _host_label (the host and port, lower-cased) is the domain label at all three sites; _site (the host after the last @, without its port or www.; written in the module so it does not load src.ingest, R621, and held equal to src.ingest.crawl._registrable_host by a test) decides internal: same-host spellings are internal and are no longer stored as outbound links; another host stays external; two empty hosts are no site. (2) feed_key drops the userinfo; read_feed_key reads a stored key holding an @ as its row's feed key today (exact: a key written since R628 holds an @ only where it is not a userinfo, and re-deriving gives it back). (3) canonicalize_url drops the userinfo (url-v2); CANON_VERSION moves url-v1 -> url-v2 by its own rule (bump whenever canonicalize_url changes its rules); the boot self-heal that backfills canon_version on rows predating the column now writes url-v1, as the Alembic revision d3e4f5a6b7c8 does (CANON_VERSION alone would have stamped url-v1 rows url-v2). (4) the preflight's host is the fetcher's host key (_host_netloc with the URL's scheme: lower-cased, its default port gone), so the report and the robots read carry no userinfo; the sampled feed itself is still fetched as given. The page request everywhere still carries the URL as written (R621). CONTINUITY, per stored identity: articles.canonical_url (indexed, not unique; written by pipeline/batch from canonicalize_url; read by the pre-fetch dedup in ingest_url and the crawl, the in-memory dedup front, link_preview's lookup; evidence bundles, custody records and the runlog export carry the stored value, never recompute it): rows stored before R628 keep their canonical_url, credentials included, and their url-v1 stamp; nothing rewrites them. Without a fallback, an article stored from a credentialed URL would be fetched again on every pass that lists it (the content hash then names it a duplicate, after the request; a changed page would be stored a second time). Fallback added: pipeline._canonical_stored, used by ingest_url and the crawl, asks url_v1_canonical's form on a miss, only for a URL whose authority holds an @ (one indexed query; the dedup front is not marked with it, so it stays exact). Stated: link_preview for the plain URL does not find an article whose stored canonical_url holds credentials (it still matches Article.url as given). sources.feed_key (UNIQUE (domain, feed_key); derived on every ORM write by the before_insert/before_update event, re-derived by the source-topics bulk UPDATE and the curated-stamp heal; read by source_lookup's add and YAML-import lookups, the CSV import, the seeder's pairing and the restore merge's SQL join): a key stored before R628 stays until its row's next ORM write (an edit, enable/disable, a qualification verdict, the crawl's last_crawled_at stamp), which re-derives it without the userinfo. Fallback added: read_feed_key in source_for_feed (only on a miss, only the domain's keys holding an @), source_for_import and csv_io.upsert_sources, so adding or importing the same feed again edits the legacy row instead of making a second one. Not added, stated: the restore merge compares the stored column in SQL (a domain with one source on each side still matches by its one-to-one fallback; with several, an incoming copy of a local legacy-keyed feed lands as a new sibling until the local row heals), and the seeder compares stored keys (the bundled catalogue holds no credentialed URL, so a legacy key never matched a catalogue entry and still does not; once healed, a credentialed operator row pairs with the catalogue entry of the same feed and the three-way merge keeps the operator's URL). Cost that cannot be kept cheaply, because it is the ruling's dedup itself: a domain that already holds ONE feed twice (once with credentials and once without, or with two logins; possible before because the keys differed) now derives one key for both, so the credentialed row's next ORM write fails UNIQUE (domain, feed_key) (the crawl supplement logs the failure and the outlet's stamp is rolled back, so it is due again next rotation), the daily source-topics bulk UPDATE fails whole if it writes such a row, and restoring a backup holding such a pair into a store holding neither fails at the source INSERT; the remedy is deleting one of the two rows. The count is unknown; it needs an operator-added second row naming a feed the store already held, with a login. The preflight host: data/feed_preflight.jsonl is a log; its records' host values are written at run time, and the bundled market, index and calendar catalogues hold no credentialed URL, so no stored record has one. The extractor's domain label is not stored; ArticleLink rows already stored from same-host links stay (links are extracted only at ingest). ENGINE STAMP: tests/test_index_engine_stamp.py: the canonical URL and the feed key are not index inputs (index_inputs_digest reads text, title, languages, date, country and self-name forms); feed_key.py is NOT_OUTPUT_AFFECTING (a pass loads it, never writes sources) and gains no import, so the closure, the pins and INDEXER_VERSION are unchanged. IMPORT COST: no new import in the extractor, url_utils, feed_key or source_lookup (pure string helpers); feed_preflight already imported src.ingest at top level; a fresh-interpreter test pins that the four still import without src.ingest. TESTS: tests/test_userinfo_labels_r628.py, 107 cases, through the real crawl_source and ingest_url over an in-memory session, _maybe_index_links, create_source, upsert_sources, the YAML import, merge_corpus and run_feed_preflight. On 6dd9b14fe (the R624 fold) 36 bug cases fail, the 35 cases of the three new helpers (_site, read_feed_key, url_v1_canonical) fail because they do not exist there, and the 30 controls and 6 continuity cases pass; on this branch all 107 pass. 437 related existing test files, test_index_engine_stamp.py and test_article_identity_seams.py among them: 9,141 passed; the two failures (test_shared_file_writes on src/ingest/__init__.py's three unconverted write sites, and test_source_coverage_rollup's mean-tone case, this venv lacking vaderSentiment) fail the same way on 6dd9b14fe, in files this change does not touch; test_awareness.py and test_commodity.py were left out, as this venv cannot import them (vaderSentiment, scipy). MUTANTS: 32, each undoing one part (the label in _host_label and at its three sites; the internal compare; _site's last-@ cut, its www., its as-written fallback and its empty-host guard; feed_key's cut; read_feed_key both ways; the add, YAML and CSV fallbacks; the canonical cut and _authority_host; the two readers; the version bump; url_v1_canonical three ways; the url-v1 backfill; the pipeline fallback and its two call sites; the preflight host two ways; a top-level src.ingest import in the extractor, feed_key and url_utils): all killed. NOT CHANGED, stated: the extractor's normalize_url still keeps a cross-host link's userinfo in ArticleLink.normalized_url, a stored identity read by co-citation, link_preview and the articles-by-link lookup (not one of the four places; it needs its own continuity read); the url column of each preflight record still holds the feed URL as given; feed_key's fallback for a URL urllib.parse cannot read keeps its lower-cased text, userinfo included; Article.url and ArticleLink.url keep the URL as given (data handed back, R621). Release-notes line: «A user name and password written into a web address no longer become part of how the app recognises a page, a feed or a site: the same page or feed written with and without them is now one, they no longer reach a stored article's canonical address or the feed check's report, and a link to an article's own site written with a login, a port or "www." is no longer counted as a link to another site. (R628)»
